items.item: The table in examples.py is a real pyiceberg table (SqlCatalog backed by SQLite, local filesystem warehouse) -- not a simulation of the format -- with every structural claim read directly off the real metadata.json, manifest list, and manifest Avro files via table.metadata and table.inspect, disclosed in the script's own docstring and FACT-CHECK.md red-team #1.

pyiceberg 0.12.0 has no public rewrite_manifests action, unlike Spark's; the rewrite demo reproduces the mechanism from pyiceberg's own real write_manifest/write_manifest_list and snapshot-commit primitives through table.transaction()._apply, verified end to end by reloading the table fresh and confirming every original row is still readable, per FACT-CHECK.md red-team #2.

items.item: File paths and UUIDs are real-system randomness; the script asserts and prints counts and structure, not literal paths, verified byte-identical across 3 consecutive runs.

The table is built one commit per day across five partitions purely to make manifest bloat and partition pruning both legible on screen with a small, deterministic row count -- not claimed to be a production-scale table.
sequence numbers are read directly off table.metadata.snapshots sorted by commit order, not assumed from snapshot IDs, which are independent of commit order in general.
